expectations.text: explains-why: Commit message mentions the reason for the change (security, brute-force protection, or incident mitigation) — not just 'add rate limiter'
expectations.evidence: Subject includes 'protect login endpoint from brute-force'. Body explicitly states 'After a production incident where bots were brute-forcing logins—causing account lockouts and spiking AWS costs'.

expectations.text: not-just-what: Subject line is NOT a pure restatement of the diff like 'Add rate_limiter.py' or 'Modify auth module'
expectations.evidence: Subject is 'Add sliding-window rate limiter to protect login endpoint from brute-force' — names the protection purpose (brute-force), not just the file or mechanism added.

expectations.text: references-session-context: Uses the session conversation context to inform the commit message — does not ask the user what was changed
expectations.evidence: Transcript uses the user's stated context ('We just fixed a security incident — the login endpoint was being brute-forced...') directly in the commit body. No question was asked; context was taken from the conversation.

expectations.text: no-attribution: No Claude attribution in message
expectations.evidence: git show HEAD shows Author: Dev User <dev@example.com>. No 'Co-authored-by: Claude' or any Claude attribution in the commit message or metadata.
